'''Nikodem Janusz Popławski''' (born March 1, 1975) is a Polish [[theoretical physicist]], most widely noted for the hypothesis that every [[black hole]] could be a doorway to another universe and that the [[universe]] was formed within a black hole which itself exists in a larger universe.<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20100414233609/http://news.nationalgeographic.com/news/2010/04/100409-black-holes-alternate-universe-multiverse-einstein-wormholes/ National Geographic Daily News: "Every Black Hole Contains Another Universe?"]<br />[https://www.science.org/content/article/does-our-universe-live-inside-wormhole Science News: "Does Our Universe Live Inside a Wormhole?"]<br />[http://www.space.com/scienceastronomy/universe-born-in-black-hole-100427.html Space.com: "Our Universe Was Born in a Black Hole, Theory Says"]<br />[https://www.newscientist.com/article/mg20727703.000-every-black-hole-may-hold-a-hidden-universe.html "Every black hole may hold a hidden universe"] in ''[[New Scientist]]'', Vol. 207, No. 2770, p. 9 (2010)<br />[https://web.archive.org/web/20140221201026/http://news.nationalgeographic.com/news/2014/02/140218-black-hole-blast-explains-big-bang/ National Geographic Daily News: "Are We Living in a Black Hole?"]<br />[https://www.bbc.co.uk/teach/articles/zjn68xs BBC iWonder: "How do we know the Big Bang actually happened?"]<br />[http://www.smithsonianmag.com/science/what-universe-real-physics-has-some-mind-bending-answers-180952699/?no-ist Smithsonian: "What Is the Universe? Real Physics Has Some Mind-Bending Answers"]</ref> This hypothesis was listed by ''[[National Geographic (magazine)|National Geographic]]'' and ''[[Science (magazine)|Science]]'' magazines among their ten most-read stories of 2010.<ref name="NG2010">[https://web.archive.org/web/20101203053822/http://news.nationalgeographic.com/news/2010/11/photogalleries/101130-best-of-2010-science-nature-pictures-news-fish-hands National Geographic Daily News: "Top Ten Discoveries of 2010: Nat Geo News's Most Popular"]</ref><ref name="Science2010">[https://www.science.org/content/article/top-10-sciencenows-2010 Science News: "Top 10 ScienceNOWs of 2010"]</ref>

== Black holes are edgeways ==
Popławski's approach is based on the [[Einstein–Cartan theory]] of gravity which extends [[general relativity]] to matter with intrinsic [[angular momentum]] ([[Spin (physics)|spin]]).  Spin in curved [[spacetime]] requires that the [[affine connection]] cannot be constrained to zero and its antisymmetric part, the [[torsion tensor]], must be a variable in [[Hamilton's principle]] of stationary action which gives the field equations.  Torsion gives the correct generalization of the conservation law for the total (orbital plus intrinsic) angular momentum to the presence of the gravitational field, but also modifies the [[Nonlinear Dirac equation|Dirac equation]] for [[fermion]]s.

Gravitational effects of torsion on fermionic matter are significant at extremely high densities which exist inside black holes and at the beginning of the Universe.  Popławski theorizes that torsion manifests itself as a repulsive force which causes fermions to be spatially extended and prevents the formation of a [[gravitational singularity]] within the black hole's [[event horizon]].<ref>{{cite journal | author=N. J. Popławski | date=2010 | title=Nonsingular Dirac particles in spacetime with torsion | journal=Physics Letters B | volume=690 | issue=1 | pages=73–77 | doi=10.1016/j.physletb.2010.04.073 | arxiv=0910.1181 | bibcode=2010PhLB..690...73P}}</ref>  Because of torsion, the collapsing matter on the other side of the horizon reaches an enormous but finite density, explodes and rebounds, forming an Einstein-Rosen bridge ([[wormhole]]) to a new, closed, expanding universe.<ref>{{cite journal | author=N. J. Popławski | date=2010 | title=Radial motion into an Einstein-Rosen bridge | journal=Physics Letters B | volume=687 | issue=2–3 | pages=110–113 | doi=10.1016/j.physletb.2010.03.029 | arxiv=0902.1994 | bibcode=2010PhLB..687..110P| s2cid=5947253 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | author=N. J. Popławski | date=2010 | title=Cosmology with torsion: An alternative to cosmic inflation | journal=Physics Letters B | volume=694 | issue=3 | pages=181–185 | doi=10.1016/j.physletb.2010.09.056 | arxiv=1007.0587 | bibcode=2010PhLB..694..181P}}</ref>  Quantum particle production in strong gravitational fields helps torsion to overcome [[Shear stress|shear]].<ref>{{cite journal | author=N. Popławski | date=2021 | title=Гравитационный коллапс жидкого объекта с кручением с образованием вселенной в черной дыре | journal=Zhurnal Eksperimental'noi i Teoreticheskoi Fiziki | volume=159 | issue=3 | pages=448–456 | doi=10.31857/S0044451021030068 | arxiv=2008.02136| s2cid=234355453 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | author=N. Popławski | date=2021 | title=Gravitational collapse of a fluid with torsion into a universe in a black hole | journal=Journal of Experimental and Theoretical Physics | volume=132 | issue=3 | pages=374–380 | doi=10.1134/S1063776121030092 | arxiv=2008.02136| bibcode=2021JETP..132..374N }}</ref><ref>{{cite book | author=N. Popławski | date=2023 | chapter=Chapter 13: Gravitational Collapse with Torsion and Universe in a Black Hole | editor=C. Bambi | title=Regular Black Holes: Towards a New Paradigm of Gravitational Collapse | publisher=Springer | pages=485–499 | doi=10.1007/978-981-99-1596-5_13 | arxiv=2307.12190 }}</ref>  Analogously, the [[Big Bang]] is replaced by the [[Big Bounce]] before which the Universe was the interior of a black hole.<ref>{{cite journal | author=N. Popławski | date=2012 | title=Nonsingular, big-bounce cosmology from spinor-torsion coupling | journal=Physical Review D | volume=85 | issue=10 | article-number=107502 | doi=10.1103/PhysRevD.85.107502 | arxiv=1111.4595| bibcode=2012PhRvD..85j7502P | s2cid=118434253 }}</ref>  This scenario generates [[cosmic inflation]], which explains why the present Universe at largest scales appears spatially flat, [[homogeneous]] and [[isotropic]].<ref>{{cite journal | author=N. Popławski | date=2016 | title=Universe in a black hole in Einstein-Cartan gravity | journal=Astrophysical Journal | volume=832 | issue=2 | page=96 | doi=10.3847/0004-637X/832/2/96 | arxiv=1410.3881| bibcode=2016ApJ...832...96P | s2cid=119771613 | doi-access=free }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | author=G. Unger, N. Popławski | date=2019 | title=Big Bounce and closed Universe from spin and torsion | journal=Astrophysical Journal | volume=870 | issue=2 | page=78 | doi=10.3847/1538-4357/aaf169 | arxiv=1808.08327| bibcode=2019ApJ...870...78U | s2cid=119514549 | doi-access=free }}</ref>  It may explain the [[arrow of time]], solve the [[black hole information paradox]], and explain the nature of [[dark matter]].<ref>{{cite journal | author=N. J. Popławski | date=2014 | title=The energy and momentum of the Universe | journal=Classical and Quantum Gravity | volume=31 | issue=6 | article-number=065005 | doi=10.1088/0264-9381/31/6/065005 | arxiv=1305.6977| bibcode=2014CQGra..31f5005P | s2cid=118593046 }}</ref>  Torsion may also be responsible for the observed asymmetry between matter and [[antimatter]] in the Universe.<ref>{{cite journal | author=N. J. Popławski | date=2011 | title=Matter-antimatter asymmetry and dark matter from torsion | journal=Physical Review D | volume=83 | issue=8 | article-number=084033 | doi=10.1103/PhysRevD.83.084033 | arxiv=1101.4012| bibcode=2011PhRvD..83h4033P | s2cid=119223239 }}</ref> The rotation of a black hole could influence the spacetime on the other side of its event horizon and result in a preferred direction in the new universe.  Popławski suggests that the observed fluctuations in the [[cosmic microwave background]] might provide evidence for his hypothesis.<ref>{{cite journal | author=S. Desai, N. J. Popławski | date=2016 | title=Non-parametric reconstruction of an inflaton potential from Einstein–Cartan–Sciama–Kibble gravity with particle production | journal=Physics Letters B | volume=755 | pages=183–189 | doi=10.1016/j.physletb.2016.02.014 | arxiv=1510.08834 | bibcode=2016PhLB..755..183D| s2cid=55366841 }}</ref>

Popławski proposed that the [[momentum]] components do not [[Commutator|commute]] in the presence of torsion.  Accordingly, integration over the continuous momentum in [[Feynman diagram]]s is replaced with summation over the discrete momentum [[Eigenvalues and eigenvectors|eigenvalues]] whose separation increases with magnitude.  Consequently, divergent integrals in Feynman diagrams are replaced with convergent sums.  Therefore, torsion might eliminate [[ultraviolet divergence]] and provide a physical mechanism for [[Regularization (physics)|regularization]] in [[quantum field theory]], giving finite values of [[Renormalization|bare]] quantities such as the [[mass]] and [[electric charge]] of the [[electron]].<ref>{{cite journal | author=N. Popławski | date=2020 | title=Noncommutative momentum and torsional regularization | journal=Foundations of Physics | volume=50 | issue=9 | pages=900–923 | doi=10.1007/s10701-020-00357-1 | arxiv=1712.09997| bibcode=2020FoPh...50..900P | s2cid=220511295 }}</ref>

He also proposed that the [[four-velocity]] of a fermion ([[spinor]]) particle is related to its relativistic [[wave function]].  For a curved spacetime with torsion, the [[four-momentum]] of a spinor is related to a generator of [[translation (geometry)|translation]], given by a [[covariant derivative]], and the [[relativistic angular momentum|four-angular momentum]] is related to a generator of [[rotation]] in the [[Lorentz group]].  From the covariant [[conservation law|conservation laws]] for the [[spin tensor]] and [[stress-energy tensor|energy–momentum tensor]] for a spinor field in the presence of torsion, it follows that if the wave satisfies the [[Dirac equation in curved spacetime|curved]] Dirac equation, then the four-velocity, four-momentum, and four-spin satisfy the [[Mathisson–Papapetrou–Dixon equations|Mathisson–Papapetrou equations]] of motion, which reduce to the [[geodesics in general relativity|geodesic equation]].  Consequently, the motion of a particle guided by the four-velocity in the [[de Broglie–Bohm theory|pilot wave]] interpretation of [[quantum mechanics]] coincides with the geodesic motion determined by spacetime, demonstrating a relativistic [[wave–particle duality]].<ref>{{cite journal | author=F. R. Benard Guedes, N. J. Popławski | date=2024 | title=General-relativistic wave–particle duality with torsion | journal=Classical and Quantum Gravity | volume=41 | issue=6 | page=065011 | doi=10.1088/1361-6382/ad1fcb | arxiv=2211.03234 }}</ref>

== Education ==
Popławski received his M.Sc. degree in astronomy from the [[University of Warsaw]] (1999), and his Ph.D. degree in physics from [[Indiana University]] (2004), where he later worked as a lecturer and researcher in theoretical physics.  He joined the Department of Mathematics and Physics at the [[University of New Haven]] as a senior lecturer in 2013 and became a distinguished lecturer in 2020.

==In popular culture==
Popławski appeared in an episode of the TV show ''[[Through the Wormhole]]'' titled "Are There Parallel Universes?" (season 2) and in an episode of the [[Discovery Channel]] show ''[[Curiosity (TV series)|Curiosity]]'' titled "Is There a Parallel Universe?",<ref name="IMDb">[https://www.imdb.com/name/nm4709263/ Nikodem Poplawski - IMDb"]</ref> which aired in 2011.
